Image is for illustrative purposes onlyand does not represent a specific brandWhen I first started working in a pharmacy

three years ago I made the same mistake that

most of my customers still make today.

I thought melatonin was a vitamin. Or maybe

a mineral. Something you take to fill a

nutritional gap.

I was completely wrong.

And understanding what melatonin actually is

changed everything about how I explain it to

customers — and why it works better for sleep

than almost anything else we stock.

---

So What Exactly Is Melatonin?

Melatonin is not a vitamin.

Melatonin is not a mineral.

Melatonin is not a herbal supplement.

Melatonin is a hormone.

Specifically it is a hormone that your own

body already produces naturally — made by a

tiny gland in your brain called the pineal

gland.

Your body starts producing melatonin

naturally when it gets dark outside. It is

your body's own internal signal that says

"it is nighttime — time to sleep."

When you take a melatonin supplement you are

not giving your body something foreign. You

are giving it more of something it already

makes itself.

This is why melatonin works differently from

any other sleep supplement.

---

Why Melatonin Works Better for Sleep Than

Vitamins or Minerals

When customers ask me for a sleep supplement

I always ask them one question first.

"Do you struggle to fall asleep — or do you

struggle to stay asleep?"

If the answer is falling asleep — melatonin

is almost always my first recommendation.

Here is why:

Magnesium Glycinate helps your body and

muscles relax. It creates the right conditions

for sleep. But it does not send a direct

sleep signal to your brain.

Melatonin sends a direct signal to your brain

that it is time to sleep. It works with your

body's own natural system — not against it.

This is the difference that matters.

---

Who Benefits Most From Melatonin

From my three years of pharmacy experience

the customers who benefit most from melatonin

are very specific:

1. Shift Workers

People who work night shifts or rotating

schedules completely confuse their body's

natural melatonin production. Their brain

does not know when it is supposed to be day

or night. Melatonin supplements help reset

this cycle.

This is extremely common among expat workers

in Qatar who work long or irregular hours.

2. People With Jet Lag

Travelling across time zones throws your

natural melatonin timing completely off.

A low dose of melatonin taken at the correct

local bedtime helps reset your internal clock

faster than anything else.

3. People Who Cannot Fall Asleep

If you lie in bed for an hour before finally

falling asleep — your natural melatonin

production may simply be delayed or

insufficient. A small supplement dose taken

30 minutes before bed can fix this quickly.

4. People Who Stare at Screens at Night

Blue light from phones and laptops blocks

your brain from producing melatonin

naturally. If you use your phone until

midnight and then wonder why you cannot

sleep — this is exactly why.

---

What Most People Get Wrong About Melatonin

This is the most important section I want

every customer to read.

Mistake 1 — Taking too high a dose

More melatonin does not mean better sleep.

Research consistently shows that lower doses

— between 0.5mg and 3mg — work better than

high doses of 10mg that many products

contain. Higher doses can actually disrupt

your natural hormone production over time.

Mistake 2 — Taking it at the wrong time

Melatonin must be taken 30 minutes before

your intended sleep time. Taking it too early

or too late significantly reduces its

effectiveness.

Mistake 3 — Using it every single night

long term

Melatonin is most effective for short term

use — helping reset your sleep schedule.

Using it every night indefinitely is not

recommended without medical guidance as your

body may reduce its own natural production.

Mistake 4 — Expecting it to keep you asleep

Melatonin helps you fall asleep. It does not

necessarily keep you asleep all night. If

your problem is waking up at 3am —

Magnesium Glycinate may actually serve you

better.

---

Melatonin vs Magnesium Glycinate —

Which One Do You Need?

This is the question I answer most often

when customers cannot decide between the two.

CHOOSE MELATONIN IF:

✓ You struggle to fall asleep

✓ You are a shift worker

✓ You have jet lag

✓ Your sleep schedule is irregular

✓ You use your phone late at night

CHOOSE MAGNESIUM GLYCINATE IF:

✓ You wake up multiple times at night

✓ You feel anxious or stressed daily

✓ Your muscles feel tense before bed

✓ You want long term daily support

CONSIDER BOTH IF:

✓ You struggle to fall asleep AND stay asleep

✓ You have high daily stress AND poor sleep

Many customers use a low dose of each

together with good results.

---

Important Warnings

Because melatonin is a hormone — not just a

supplement — there are important cautions:

- Children and teenagers should only use

 melatonin under direct medical supervision

- Pregnant and breastfeeding women should

 avoid melatonin without doctor guidance

- People taking blood thinners, diabetes

 medication, or immune suppressants should

 consult their doctor first

- Do not drive or operate machinery after

 taking melatonin

My Honest Pharmacy Observation

Melatonin is one of the fastest acting sleep

supplements we stock. Most customers who use

it correctly — right dose, right timing —

notice a real difference within the first

few nights.

But the keyword is correctly.

Most people take too much, too late, and

expect miracles. Follow the basics I outlined

above and melatonin genuinely delivers.

DISCLAIMER:

I am a pharmacy assistant not a licensed
